newsitem.title: ITALY: Fazio hopes for Italy rate cut, but outlook cloudy.
newsitem.headline: Fazio hopes for Italy rate cut, but outlook cloudy.

text.p: Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said on Thursday he hoped he would be able to cut interest rates but warned that the outlook appeared unsettled.
Fazio told a parliamentary commission that if he cut short-term rates there were not the conditions for a corresponding fall in market rates.
"This would be very dangerous," he said. "I hope to be able to do it but the weather forecast is rather disturbed."
Unions and business leaders have been urging the Bank of Italy to cut rates in recent months to help boost the flagging economy.
"I have not cut rates because I thought that there were some extremely difficult passages (to overcome)," Fazio told the parliamentary commission.
"The lira, thank God, has not been involved, but this does not mean that it won't be in the future," he added.
He added that monetary policy had remained tight because the markets were not convinced about the long-term sustainability of the Italian economy.
But he said he also had to bear in mind Italy's snarled economy, which slowed in 0.5 percent year-on-year in the first quarter of 1997. "There has to be more growth," Fazio said.
Italy's official discount rate has been held at 6.75 percent since mid-January, despite a sharp fall in inflation.. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
